# Native paired rendering and NVIDIA MVR

User request: implement real SPS/instanced stereo and NVIDIA multi-view rendering to reduce CPU rendering work. Work starts from verified 0.4.0 commit d275dbd on research/sps-mvr; the 0.4.0 release candidate and unrelated edits stay in their original checkout.

Design: preserve the existing native path as the fallback. A portable paired backend already exists; add a NVIDIA backend using real custom-semantic shaders and verified mode transitions. Prove four asymmetric color/depth outputs against four native reference draws before integrating any game draw suppression. Capability query or successful mode-set alone is not correctness proof.

Native integration must own all paired intermediate outputs and mutable inputs through their consumers. Evaluate outer/focus pairing within one eye first, since their poses match and this avoids waiting for the right-eye scene. Shared preparation needs conservative visibility and preserved native bookkeeping. Do not replay borrowed view pointers or suppress unknown work.

Plan:
- [ ] NVIDIA SPS/MVR backend, injectable API contracts, asymmetric hardware equivalence and mode restoration tests.
- [ ] Native pass ownership/scheduling analysis; implement a bounded scheduler and resource lifecycle tests for a proven supported subset.
- [ ] Shader and draw integration with complete fallback before visible mutation; measure eliminated native preparation/draws.
- [ ] Offline hardware/game visual tests, followed by matched CPU A/B. User handles cockpit/headset and hotkey; use 30-second captures and close LMU afterward.

No signing during development; no anti-cheat changes; no release/UI claim of working SPS/MVR until the native path actually replaces duplicate work and passes image comparison.

The desktop managed-worktree tool did not return and was stopped before creating a checkout. A normal Git worktree was created at the explicitly selected research directory as fallback.
